changes.reason: Adds a server integration subpath with finite classification/review contracts and a stateful service using node:crypto, an injected store and application-owned authorization/PII policy. The package catalog has no runtime claim; Node tests and the loopback example do not establish a selected infrastructure Host/Profile.

kubernetes.reason: The service executes in the Node reference path, but no Kubernetes/Node Host composition or deployment Profile is selected for this capability. The catalog remains runtime-unclaimed.
constraints: Requires a Node-compatible crypto implementation and current application-owned authorization/PII/source checks.
The application owns durable event/usage sinks, PostgreSQL lifecycle and deployment; no cluster verification or provider certification is claimed.

aws-lambda.reason: No Lambda Host/invocation-boundary integration was executed for the server subpath, and the catalog does not claim Lambda support.
constraints: A selected Lambda composition must preserve invocation scope and settle/flush durable event and usage delivery before returning.
Unknown provider acceptance retains its reservation; a stopped-worker acknowledgement never makes retries exactly-once or bypasses attempt limits.
The example in-memory sinks and long-running HTTP server do not establish Lambda lifecycle behavior.

cloudflare.reason: The subpath imports node:crypto and has no selected Workers Host, compatible durable store or runtime capability declaration. No Workers compatibility mode or Node Container composition was exercised.
constraints: Do not infer Worker-isolate support from Node tests or Node Container availability.
An application must supply and validate compatible crypto, durable storage, authorization/PII policy and resource lifecycle before making a Workers claim.

changes.reason: Adds PostgreSQL run/CAS storage, immutable-source receipts and an explicit enrichment migration using the existing injected Drizzle database contract. Reuses the catalogued Node/Lambda provider rather than introducing platform-specific stores.

kubernetes.reason: The existing Node/PostgreSQL provider is reusable with application-managed PostgreSQL connections and an explicit migration; cluster deployment is not validated.
constraints: Run createEnrichment explicitly before serving traffic; importing or booting the store does not own schema migration.
The application owns PostgreSQL availability, credentials, bounded connection pooling and rollout/close behavior.
Local real-PostgreSQL CAS/restart tests are not a Kubernetes cluster test or production certification; end-to-end Host integration remains unverified in the analytics-core record.

aws-lambda.reason: The catalogued Lambda provider requires an application-selected connection lifecycle and invocation-scoped execution; this store adds no Lambda Host integration.
constraints: Reuse or close PostgreSQL resources according to the selected Lambda Host and provider contract; bound connections and concurrent invocations.
Apply the migration separately; preserve CAS leases, immutable input revisions and unknown-acceptance receipts across cold starts.
Flush/settle application-owned durable sinks before invocation return; in-memory reference sinks are not durable across cold starts.
No AWS invocation, deployment or production provider certification was executed for this change.

cloudflare.reason: The selected PostgreSQL provider catalog claims Node and Lambda, not Workers. This change includes no Workers storage Provider or Host integration.
constraints: This decision covers Workers isolates; the Node/PostgreSQL example must not be treated as a Workers deployment.
A Cloudflare Node Container is a separate Node Host choice and remains unverified here; it is not a Worker isolate.
